calls.body: The Red Wings’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Rangers’ power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Red Wings tonight.

calls.head: Forecheck against patience
calls.body: On forecheck pressure, the Rangers are one of the league’s best, but Detroit is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect the Rangers to win more pucks back deep in the Red Wings’ end.

surprises.head: Dylan Garand stole one with a shutout
surprises.body: Garand stopped all 22 shots, worth 1.6 expected goals. That is more than the Rangers’ winning margin, not counting empty-net goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 7 starts.

story.head: Garand blanks the Red Wings
paras: Sean Durzi scored his first goal for the Rangers on the power play early in the first to open the scoring. The Rangers had a goal taken off for offside midway through the period, but it didn’t cost them in the end. Durzi and Marco Kasper fought midway through the second. Eeli Tolvanen sealed it into the empty net with a little over a minute left.

The Rangers had a bit more of the good stuff. Dylan Garand made 22 saves for his first NHL shutout. John Gibson stopped 19 of 20 for the Red Wings. The Rangers improved to 2-1-0, and the Wings fell to 0-1-0.
